# nxos_msdp (Resource)

This resource can manage the MSDP (Multicast Source Discovery Protocol) configuration on NX-OS devices, including per-VRF settings, peers, mesh groups, SA policies, group limits and redistribution.

### API Documentation

- [msdpEntity](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:Entity/)
- [msdpInst](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:Inst/)
- [msdpDom](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:Dom/)
- [msdpPeer](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:Peer/)
- [msdpAuthP](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:AuthP/)
- [msdpMeshGrp](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:MeshGrp/)
- [msdpRtCtrlP](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:RtCtrlP/)
- [msdpMaxGrpP](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:MaxGrpP/)
- [msdpInterLeakP](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Discovery%20Protocols/msdp:InterLeakP/)

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nxos_msdp" "example" {
  admin_state          = "enabled"
  instance_admin_state = "enabled"
  instance_control     = "stateful-ha"
  vrfs = {
    "default" = {
      control                = "flush-routes"
      originator_interface   = "lo0"
      reconnect_interval     = 20
      source_active_interval = 100
      peers = {
        "10.1.1.2" = {
          admin_state                = "disabled"
          remote_as                  = "65001"
          description                = "My MSDP peer"
          keepalive_interval         = 30
          keepalive_timeout          = 60
          name                       = "peer1"
          source_active_limit        = 1000
          source_interface           = "lo0"
          authentication_description = "My authentication description"
          authentication_key         = "secret_key"
          authentication_keychain    = "KC1"
          authentication_name        = "auth1"
          authentication_type        = "md5"
          mesh_group_description     = "My mesh group description"
          mesh_group_name            = "MESH1"
          mesh_group_policy_name     = "mesh1"
          sa_policies = {
            "in" = {
              description = "My SA policy"
              name        = "sa-policy"
              route_map   = "SA_POLICY"
            }
          }
        }
      }
      group_limits = {
        "10.0.0.0/8" = {
          description    = "My group limit"
          maximum_groups = 100
          name           = "group-limit"
        }
      }
      redistribution_description = "My redistribution"
      redistribution_name        = "redist"
      redistribution_route_map   = "REDIST"
      redistribution_scope       = "inter"
      redistribution_source      = "rtmap"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `deletion_policy` (String) What happens on the device when objects managed by the resource are removed. `delete` deletes the object on destroy, including any configuration not managed by Terraform, and deletes single child objects once none of their attributes are configured anymore, unless the device holds other entries below them. `reset` deletes the objects created by the resource on destroy, resets the managed attributes of the objects that already existed and leaves configuration not managed by Terraform in place. `retain` leaves the device unchanged on destroy and only removes the resource from the state. Overrides the `deletion_policy` of the provider, which defaults to `delete`. See the [Deletion Policy](../guides/deletion_policy) guide for details.
  - Choices: `delete`, `reset`, `retain`
- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.
- `instance_admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `instance_control` (String) The control state.
  - Choices: `stateful-ha`
- `vrfs` (Attributes Map) List of MSDP VRF configurations.
  - Map key: `name` - VRF name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The distinguished name of the object.

<a id="nestedatt--vrfs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vrfs`

Optional:

- `control` (String) Flush routes.
  - Choices: `flush-routes`
- `group_limits` (Attributes Map) List of MSDP group limits per source prefix.
  - Map key: `source_prefix` - Source prefix. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs--group_limits))
- `originator_interface` (String) Originator Interface identifying IP address in RP field of Source-Active message. Supported interfaces include Ethernet-like, port/channel, loopback and vlan interfaces.
- `peers` (Attributes Map) List of MSDP peers.
  - Map key: `address` - IP address of MSDP Peer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs--peers))
- `reconnect_interval` (Number) Reconnect Interval.
  - Range: `1`-`60`
- `redistribution_description` (String) Description of the specified attribute.
- `redistribution_name` (String) Object name.
- `redistribution_prefix_list` (String) pfxlist name.
- `redistribution_route_map` (String) The name of the default route leak policy route map. This route map name is used to control distribution.
- `redistribution_scope` (String) The domain applicable to the capability.
  - Choices: `intra`, `inter`, `defrt`
- `redistribution_source` (String) Source of route leak distribution.
  - Choices: `none`, `pflist`, `rtmap`
- `source_active_interval` (Number) Source Active message Interval.
  - Range: `60`-`65535`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = nxos_msdp.example
  identity = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema


#### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform's `import` block requires a non-empty `id` value, so this format cannot be used to
# import nxos_msdp for the default device. Use the `terraform import` command
# below, or identity-based import shown above, instead.
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nxos_msdp.example ""
```
